assertions.text: Table columns represent the method's public inputs (applicant type, age, claim count) and observable outputs (decision, premium) — not internal state
assertions.evidence: Columns are 'Applicant Type', 'Age', 'Claim Count', 'Status?', 'Premium?' - no internal fields

assertions.text: No column is named after private fields or internal variables (hasActivePolicy, internalRiskScore, riskScore). The test treats the method as a black box.
assertions.evidence: Checked all column headers; none reference hasActivePolicy, internalRiskScore, or riskScore

assertions.text: Table has a scenario/description column as the leftmost column
assertions.evidence: First column in both tables is 'Scenario'

assertions.text: Column names use domain/business language — not code identifiers like 'applicantType', 'claimCount'
Scenario names describe conditions — not outcomes
assertions.evidence: 'Rejected - high risk' describes outcome, not condition. 'Auto-approved renewal' also describes outcome

assertions.text: Table has at least one column name ending with '?' (e.g. 'Decision?' or 'Premium?')
Test method body contains no if or switch statements
assertions.evidence: Method bodies contain only: evaluator.evaluateApplication() call and assertEquals()

assertions.text: Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
Test method has either a @DisplayName annotation or a method name that reads as a clear, descriptive title
If @Description is present and the text is longer than a single short line, it uses a text block (triple-quoted string). Passes if @Description is absent.
assertions.evidence: @Description annotation is not present in the output

assertions.text: Multiple tables are used, each addressing a distinct concern — not one monolithic table mixing unrelated rules.
assertions.evidence: Two separate @TableTest methods: one for 'Application status decision' and one for 'Premium calculation'

assertions.text: Each table has only the rows needed to express its concern's rules — no unnecessary permutations
assertions.evidence: Status table has 6 rows; Premium table has 6 rows - focused on each concern

assertions.text: Decision logic and premium calculation are in separate @TableTest methods
assertions.evidence: evaluatesApplicationStatus() and calculatesPremium() are two separate methods

assertions.text: Test method body does not recompute internal formulas. It only calls the public API and asserts on return value's fields.
assertions.evidence: Test bodies only call evaluateApplication() and assert on result fields; no risk score computation

assertions.text: @Description explains the test's purpose and business context — not internal formulas or implementation details. Passes if @Description absent.
assertions.evidence: @Description is not present in the output

assertions.text: Approval decision table covers the rejection boundary thoroughly: 5 claims triggers rejection, 4 claims approval. Senior vs non-senior (64 vs 65) distinction visible.
assertions.evidence: Table includes age=0,claims=5 (APPROVED) and age=10,claims=5 (REJECTED) for the 75 boundary, but lacks the 4-vs-5 claims comparison and 64-vs-65 age boundary

assertions.text: Approved premium table covers boundary effects: the premium jump from 0 to 1 claim, and premium difference at age 64 vs 65 (standard vs senior formula).
assertions.evidence: Premium table has 0-vs-2 claims (missing 1 claim), and age 65,70 vs 40 but no explicit 64-vs-65 comparison
